neutral_facts.value: The accused and the victim had a history of enmity related to a liquor shop license. The accused approached the victim on a motorcycle with a double barrelled gun. The victim was shot and fell down, after which the accused fled. The victim was taken to the hospital and later died. The accused was convicted based on eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and a dying declaration. The medical evidence showed multiple gun shot injuries, which were consistent with the eyewitness accounts. The dying declaration was recorded by a Tehsildar Magistrate without a doctor's certificate but was considered reliable due to the deceased's coherent and consistent statement.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution case was that there was previous enmity between the victim-deceased and the accused-appellant. Few months prior to the incident also, the appellant had tried to kill the deceased but at the time the deceased had managed to escape. On the day of incident, the deceased was on his way accompanied with PW-2 and PW-3. The appellant came there on a motorcycle armed with a double barrelled gun. The deceased was about 15-20 paces ahead of the rest. When the deceased saw the appellant advancing towards him, he tried to run. The appellant fired one shot from his double barrelled gun at the deceased. The deceased got injured and fell down. The appellant thereafter ran away leaving behind his motorcycle.

defence_argument.value: The appellant's counsel submitted that both the trial court as well as the High Court have committed a serious error in convicting the appellant for the murder. The entire genesis of the incident has been fabricated. Both the eye-witnesses PW-2 and PW-3 have stated that the appellant had fired only once from his licensed double-barrelled gun. Yet the medical evidence clearly shows that the deceased suffered multiple gun shot injuries, which are not consistent with the ocular version given by the prosecution witnesses. The motive narrated by PW-2 and PW-3 is entirely a made up story. Neither PW-2 nor PW-3 were eye-witnesses to any of the alleged incidents. They have merely given the evidence on the basis of hearsay. There was recovery of two empty cartridges from the spot which has not been explained by the prosecution.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that a dying declaration is acceptable evidence if the statement made by the injured was candid, coherent and consistent, and the deceased was in a fit state to make the statement, even if the declaration was not in question-answer form and without a certificate of fitness by a doctor.

quotes.text: The statement made by the injured was candid, coherent and consistent. There is no reason to disbelieve the same. Therefore, there is no reason to differ with the conclusions arrived at by the trial court and the High Court with regard to the dying declaration also.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed because the trial court and High Court correctly concluded that the motive was not introduced only at the time of the trial, in Court, and the medical evidence was consistent with the ocular evidence.

quotes.text: Both the trial court as well as the High Court, upon consideration of the entire ocular evidence have concluded that both PW-2 and PW-3 have given a consistent version of the various incidents narrated above, which precipitated the enmity between the deceased and the appellant.
The medical evidence is consistent with the ocular evidence. We did not see any reason to interfere with the findings recorded by both the Courts.
